name: What is the difference between a tub-to-shower conversion and a full bathroom remodel?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tub-to-shower conversion and a full bathroom remodel in cost, scope, and disruption?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a tub-to-shower conversion and a full bathroom remodel in cost, scope, and disruption?

acceptedAnswer.text: A tub-to-shower conversion is a focused project that changes one major bathing fixture and the surrounding enclosure. A full bathroom remodel goes much further, often including the vanity, toilet, flooring, lighting, ventilation, plumbing layout, paint, and sometimes walls or electrical work. Because the scope is narrower, a conversion is usually faster and less expensive than a whole-room remodel. That said, once demolition begins, contractors sometimes discover related problems that make the project feel closer to a larger remodel. Hidden water damage, outdated plumbing, or poor ventilation can expand the work. Homeowners should decide whether the goal is simply to replace the tub with a safer shower or to rework the entire bathroom experience. If only the tub is the problem, a conversion is the more efficient path. If the room is outdated in multiple ways, a full remodel may offer better long-term value despite the higher upfront cost.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tub-to-shower conversion replaces the bathtub area with a shower, while a full bathroom remodel can change the layout, fixtures, surfaces, lighting, ventilation, and storage. A conversion is usually smaller in scope, faster, and less expensive than remodeling the entire room.
